title: Intracranial EEG During Near-Threshold Detection: All-or-None Ignition Dynamics
description: Clinical iEEG test of fixed-contrast high-gamma bimodality, rapid transitions, critical slowing, long-range coherence and aINS-modulated temporal clustering; confirmatory-exploratory pending independent replication.

sub_predictions.claim: Frontoparietal cortex shows bimodal (not graded) high-gamma power at near-threshold
sub_predictions.confirming_evidence: Hartigan's dip test p < 0.05; 2-component Gaussian BIC substantially lower than 1-component (ΔBIC > 10)
sub_predictions.falsifying_evidence: Unimodal continuous distribution, established two-sided: Hartigan's dip test p > 0.20 and two-component-vs-one-component Gaussian mixture ΔBIC < 2 in favor of one component. A non-significant dip test alone does not establish unimodality. Outcomes in the intermediate band (dip p > 0.20 with 2 ≤ ΔBIC ≤ 10) are classified indeterminate and reported as such; they neither confirm nor falsify Pred 6.A.
sub_predictions.indeterminate_rule: Failure to confirm alone is not evidence of falsification. Apply the registered interval/evidence rule and admissibility gate.
sub_predictions.source: OSF Table 19, supplemented by detailed protocol decision rules below.
sub_predictions.analysis: At fixed near-threshold contrast; use nonregular mixture parametric-bootstrap LRT.

sub_predictions.claim: Intermediate-state dwell remains <15% of the 0–400 ms window (25–75% of mixture-mean separation; episodes >=100 ms). Regional specificity requires positive evidence for the occipital one-component model and a direct frontoparietal-versus-occipital contrast; a nonsignificant occipital dip test alone is indeterminate.

primary_hypothesis: Joint bimodality, brief intermediate dwell and recoverable critical-slowing evidence support transition dynamics; 6.E separately tests >=3 dissociable temporal scales in the aINS-covered subset.
primary_analysis: Single-subject hierarchical Bayesian inference BF10>=6 per prediction; group BY-FDR q=0.05. Fixed-contrast Hartigan dip plus Gaussian mixture deltaBIC and nonregular parametric-bootstrap LRT. Participant-level AC1 trend and detected/undetected permutation comparison require estimator validation before confirmatory use.

apgi_parameters.model: Reduced empirical specification: seven core quantities plus somatic modulation; not eight freely fitted parameters in every dataset.

gamma_sig.role: population-fixed model sigmoid steepness; distinct from alpha_psy

beta_SM.role: somatic modulation gain; not independently identifiable from Pi_i using behavior alone

kappa.role: energy-information bridge only; never ignition steepness

apgi_parameters.gain_interpretation: Pi_i in the reduced confirmatory model is salience-weighted gain; HEP is a candidate indicator, not a direct inverse-variance measurement.
apgi_parameters.accumulation: S_next=(1-a_S)*S+a_S*u; a_S=1-exp(-dt/tau_S); u uses calibration-fixed relative gains and excess magnitudes abs(z)-sqrt(2/pi).
apgi_parameters.ignition: p_k=1-exp(-r_max*sigmoid(gamma_sig*(S-theta))*dt); single trial-window sigmoid sampling is a distinct convention, never interchanged within a protocol.
apgi_parameters.time_step: dt=0.01 s reduced reference; dt<=min(tau_S,tau_theta,tau_Pi)/10; active reservoir additionally requires dt<=tau_res/10.
apgi_parameters.parameter_manifest_status: Required before confirmatory fitting; no unspecified coefficient is assigned a legacy default.

quality_and_decision_rules.data_admissibility: Apply registered quality gates before inference. Inadmissible data are exploratory, receive no Scenario A–F, and carry no framework vote.

scenarios.A: Scenario A — Confirmed. p < α and BF₁₀ ≥ 100. Both streams converge on H₁. Counted toward framework-level BY-FDR confirmation and toward the joint Bayesian meta-analysis. No additional replication is required before the claim is filed.
scenarios.B: Scenario B — Tentative confirmation. p < α and 3 ≤ BF₁₀ < 100. The frequentist threshold is met but Bayesian evidence is moderate rather than strong; reported as "frequentist-significant, Bayesian moderate." One pre-registered independent replication is required before the result is elevated to confirmatory status, and that replication is registered before the primary result is published.
scenarios.C: Scenario C — Discordant (frequentist-positive, Bayesian-null). p < α and BF₁₀ < 3. The frequentist threshold is met but the Bayes factor provides less than moderate evidence for H₁ and may favor H₀. Classified as equivocal: the result neither confirms nor falsifies the prediction. It is flagged as equivocal in the results and recorded in the analysis log (not in the protocol-deviation register, which is reserved for departures from registered procedure). Independent replication at ≥ 90% power is required before any interpretation is made.
scenarios.D: Scenario D — Bayesian positive (without frequentist significance). p ≥ α and BF₁₀ ≥ 100. Strong probabilistic support for H₁ while the NHST threshold is missed. Not counted toward BY-FDR (which operates on the frequentist p-values). The original study plus one pre-registered replication are required for elevation to confirmatory status.
scenarios.E: Scenario E — Bayesian falsification. p ≥ α and BF₀₁ ≥ 6. The frequentist result is nonsignificant and the Bayesian analysis supports H₀. Classified as provisional falsification of the specific sub-prediction and reported as such in the primary manuscript. A single Scenario E result triggers independent replication at ≥ 90% power before the sub-prediction is declared definitively falsified, and triggers review of whether the framework-level falsification threshold has been reached (two or more Scenario E results across primary protocols; framework-level decision rule).
scenarios.F: Scenario F — Indeterminate. p ≥ α and 1/6 < BF₁₀ < 100 (i.e., neither BF₁₀ ≥ 100 nor BF₀₁ ≥ 6). Neither stream reaches a decision threshold. Classified as inconclusive: it carries no confirmatory or falsifying weight and is reported transparently as indeterminate. It may motivate a pre-registered replication but does not by itself trigger one, and it is never counted toward BY-FDR confirmation or framework-level falsification.

quality_and_decision_rules.framework_confirmation: At least 4/5 primary protocols, combined hierarchical BF10>=100, and at most one Scenario E protocol. Protocol 0 is a gate; 2 contributes F2; 6 is CE.
quality_and_decision_rules.protocol_alpha_specification: Protocol 6 (Ignition-iEEG): Single-subject hierarchical Bayesian, BF₁₀ ≥ 6 per sub-prediction per participant. Group: Benjamini–Yekutieli FDR q = 0.05.
quality_and_decision_rules.decision_precedence: Prediction-specific estimands, interval/evidence rules and admissibility gates govern over abbreviated source summaries. The A–F matrix applies only where both frequentist and Bayesian hypotheses are explicitly defined; do not invent a point-null Bayes factor. Nonsignificance or a point estimate alone does not establish equivalence or falsification; specificity requires a direct contrast. Unresolved interval bounds or multiplicity allocations require prospective analysis lock.

submission_blocking_issues: Five samples per 50-ms AC1 window at 100 Hz: finite-sample estimator recovery and power must be archived; otherwise Pred 6.C deferred.
Absolute contrast grid in OSF conflicts with threshold-relative companion grid; OSF grid governs.
CE upgrade requires prospective amendment and independent replication in >=12 additional patients.

Final site-specific eligibility, approvals, roles, observation model and executable analysis manifest must be prospectively locked; source specification is not a completed operational study authorization.

specification_sections.heading: All-or-None Ignition Dynamics — Bistable Attractor Validation
specification_sections.text: Protocol 6 (Ignition-iEEG) tests all-or-none ignition dynamics in the frontoparietal cortex using intracranial LFP/high-gamma recordings in epilepsy patients and, where Behnke–Fried microwires are implanted, single-unit recordings.
specification_sections.role: source_context; curated structured decisions govern conflicts

specification_sections.heading: Epistemic Status Note
specification_sections.text: Given the clinical feasibility constraints of iEEG cohorts, Protocol 6 (Ignition-iEEG) is designated Confirmatory-Exploratory (CE). Target N = 20; minimum N = 12. Hypotheses Pred 6.A–Pred 6.E are treated as confirmatory within the single-subject hierarchical Bayesian framework (BF₁₀ ≥ 6 per sub-prediction — evidence for H₁; BF₀₁ is never a confirmatory criterion), but the CE designation requires independent replication in ≥ 12 additional iEEG participants before any Protocol 6 (Ignition-iEEG) result is used as standalone confirmatory evidence for APGI. CE→Confirmatory upgrade requires OSF amendment filed before replication data collection.
specification_sections.role: source_context; curated structured decisions govern conflicts

specification_sections.heading: Electrode Coverage and Stimuli
specification_sections.text: Epilepsy patients with implanted electrodes during clinical monitoring. Target coverage: frontoparietal cortex (dlPFC, PPC) and anterior insula when clinically available. Near-threshold visual detection with foveal Gabor patches (vertical, 3 cpd, 2°, 33 ms) at six contrast levels (0, 0.02, 0.04, 0.08, 0.16, 0.32), anchored by a 50-trial QUEST, with catch (25%) and suprathreshold (25%) trials. Trial structure: fixation (500 ms), stimulus (33 ms), delay (1000 ms), seen/unseen judgment plus confidence (1–4), ITI 1500–2500 ms (jittered). Primary all-patient observable: frontoparietal high-gamma/LFP under the registered signal-specific definitions; single-unit firing is analyzed only in the admissible microwire subset and reported separately; behavioral response latency is reported alongside. The six contrast values are absolute Michelson contrasts, anchored but not overwritten by the QUEST. Across the 600 trials, 150 are catch (contrast 0), 150 suprathreshold (0.32) and 300 near-threshold, spread evenly over the four intermediate contrasts (75 each); each block of 75 contains 18–19 catch, 18–19 suprathreshold and 37–38 near-threshold trials, and each attentional condition receives 300 trials in the same proportions. Interoceptive-precision modulation for Pred 6.E is implemented as a blocked attentional manipulation (eight blocks of 75 trials — four interoceptive-focus, four exteroceptive-focus — counterbalanced; 600 trials, ≥ 300 near-threshold), matching the Protocol 1 manipulation. Πⁱ state is indexed by anterior-insula high-gamma (70–150 Hz) envelope amplitude in patients with aINS coverage; patients without aINS coverage contribute to Pred 6.A–6.D only, and the Pred 6.E analysis is restricted to the aINS-covered subset with its N reported separately.
specification_sections.role: source_context; curated structured decisions govern conflicts

specification_sections.heading: iEEG-specific preprocessing by signal type
specification_sections.text: Single-unit recordings: threshold crossing at 4× RMS noise; spike sorting via Kilosort4 (Pachitariu et al., 2024); manual cluster curation in Phy; units with < 100 spikes total or < 1 Hz mean firing rate excluded. LFP recordings: bipolar re-referencing between adjacent contacts (the primary LFP reference, matched to §4.1.2), with a white-matter/common-average reference as a pre-registered sensitivity branch under identical admissibility, filtering and inference rules; no reference is selected on the basis of the ignition result; line noise removed via spectrum interpolation (local mains frequency, 50 or 60 Hz, and harmonics); bandpass filtered 1–300 Hz for broadband analysis; gamma (30–70 Hz; Table 20) and beta-band (15–30 Hz) extracted via Morlet wavelets (7 cycles). Single-unit and LFP analyses are conducted independently; cross-validation between the two measures is reported in Pred 6.A/Pred 6.E respectively.
specification_sections.role: source_context; curated structured decisions govern conflicts

specification_sections.heading: Data phases
specification_sections.text:
Phase 1 — Threshold calibration (the 50-trial QUEST): QUEST adaptive procedure establishes individual luminance threshold. These trials are excluded from primary hypothesis analyses.

Phase 2 — Main recording (minimum 300 valid trials post-calibration with ≥ 150 per detection outcome where the individual hit rate permits): All primary analyses (Pred 6.A–Pred 6.E) use Phase 2 data exclusively.

Phase 3 — Control electrode validation (concurrent with Phase 2): Occipital electrode data recorded in parallel to serve as the graded-response control for Pred 6.A/Pred 6.B bimodality tests.
specification_sections.role: source_context; curated structured decisions govern conflicts

specification_sections.heading: Real-time quality checks (iEEG)
specification_sections.text: Electrode impedance and signal quality confirmed by the clinical neurophysiology team before each recording session per standard clinical monitoring protocol. Online spike detection is checked only for the microwire/single-unit subset. Fewer than five admissible frontoparietal units affects eligibility for that subset analysis and does not exclude an otherwise admissible participant from LFP/high-gamma analyses. Unit criteria are applied before detection outcomes are unblinded, and subset counts are reported separately. Interictal discharge rate monitored online; if rate exceeds 1 per minute in target electrodes, recording is paused and clinical team notified.
specification_sections.role: source_context; curated structured decisions govern conflicts

specification_sections.heading: Competing theory predictions for Protocol 6 (Ignition-iEEG) measures
specification_sections.text: GNWT predicts late (~300 ms), all-or-none ignition with bimodal (seen/unseen) frontoparietal activity and long-range beta/gamma coherence (Dehaene et al., 2003; Sergent & Dehaene, 2004; Gaillard et al., 2009); Pred 6.A, 6.B and 6.D are therefore shared with GNWT. APGI departs from GNWT in predicting interoceptive-precision modulation of ignition timing (Pred 6.E) and a specific critical-slowing signature before detection (Pred 6.C), although stochastic GNWT models also allow spontaneous pre-stimulus fluctuations to bias ignition (Dehaene & Changeux, 2005). IIT predicts that Φ in posterior cortex, not frontoparietal coherence, best predicts seen versus unseen trials; frontoparietal coherence should be epiphenomenal. APGI predicts all-or-none bimodal dynamics (Pred 6.A), rapid transitions (Pred 6.B), critical slowing (Pred 6.C), AND frontoparietal coherence (Pred 6.D) as a jointly necessary set — no single prediction individually distinguishes APGI, but the full pattern does.
specification_sections.role: source_context; curated structured decisions govern conflicts

specification_sections.heading: Data-Admissibility Gate (EEG Trial Rejection Threshold)
specification_sections.text: Trials containing an interictal epileptiform discharge within ±500 ms of stimulus onset, or a channel amplitude |z| > 6 relative to the channel's session distribution (automated detection in the MNE-Python pipeline, confirmed by the iEEG technician), are excluded from analysis. The 30% participant-level Data-Admissibility Gate is applied uniformly across all EEG-dependent protocols and is pre-specified here to prevent analyst degrees of freedom during preprocessing. Trials rejected at the artifact-detection stage are not reconstructed and do not contribute to trial counts or statistical analysis.
specification_sections.role: source_context; curated structured decisions govern conflicts

specification_sections.heading: Pred 6.A — Bimodal firing rate distributions (all-or-none ignition)
specification_sections.text: Frontoparietal cortex shows bimodal high-gamma (70–150 Hz) power distributions in which at a fixed near-threshold contrast, a 2-component Gaussian mixture fits single-trial high-gamma amplitude better than one component (ΔBIC > 10; parametric-bootstrap likelihood-ratio test p < 0.05, because the mixture likelihood-ratio test is non-regular) and Hartigan's dip test gives p < 0.05; in microwire patients, unit firing shows separable low (≈ 5–10 spikes/s) and high (≈ 40–60 spikes/s) modes. Bimodality at fixed contrast is consistent with, but not sufficient for, bistable attractor dynamics (see Pred 6.B and 6.C). Occipital (early visual) electrodes serve as the graded-response control and are expected to show unimodal, luminance-linear distributions.
specification_sections.role: source_context; curated structured decisions govern conflicts

specification_sections.heading: Pred 6.B — Rapid transitions: dwell-time constraint AND bimodality specificity
specification_sections.text: Minimal dwell in intermediate states: the fraction of the 0–400 ms post-stimulus window spent between 25% and 75% of the separation between the two mixture-component means (episodes ≥ 100 ms) remains below 15%; dwell above 30% falsifies. Regional specificity requires positive model evidence for the registered occipital one-component alternative and a direct frontoparietal-versus-occipital contrast under the fixed model-comparison procedure. A nonsignificant occipital dip test alone is indeterminate and does not establish specificity. Bimodality alone is insufficient — a system could exhibit a bimodal distribution with slow, sticky transitions that violate the ignition requirement. The 15% dwell criterion tests transition velocity, the non-negotiable mechanistic constraint for the phase-transition claim.
specification_sections.role: source_context; curated structured decisions govern conflicts

specification_sections.heading: Two convergent measures of critical slowing, both required for full prediction confirmation:
specification_sections.text:
Behavioral (RT): Reaction times follow a quadratic fit RT ~ detection_probability + detection_probability² with negative quadratic term (p < 0.01) and RT slowest around 40–60% detection, reflecting critical fluctuations near the bifurcation point. This RT pattern is also predicted by graded-accumulation models (difficulty peaks at 50% detection) and therefore carries no discriminating weight; AC1 is the discriminating criterion.

Electrophysiological (AC1, primary): Autocorrelation (AC1) of the Sₜ proxy increases across the −500 to 0 ms pre-stimulus epoch (subsequently detected vs. undetected trials): group-median participant-level Kendall τ ≥ 0.40 (§Statistical Analysis); 0.20 ≤ τ < 0.40 is inconclusive. AC1 is the more direct dynamical signature of a saddle-node bifurcation in the iEEG signal and is the primary validation criterion; the RT prediction provides the behavioral tier for researchers without intracranial access.
specification_sections.role: source_context; curated structured decisions govern conflicts

specification_sections.heading: Pred 6.D — Long-range gamma coherence binds ignition
specification_sections.text: Beta/gamma coherence (15–80 Hz) between frontoparietal sites predicts 'seen' trials through trial-by-trial coherence correlated with detection, with point-biserial correlation r > 0.4 for frontoparietal coherence versus detection and coherence peaking 200–400 ms post-stimulus during the ignition window. This prediction links to the Global Neuronal Workspace Theory (GNWT) benchmark and enables the adversarial APGI-vs-GNWT comparison.
specification_sections.role: source_context; curated structured decisions govern conflicts

specification_sections.heading: Pred 6.E — Multi-timescale temporal clustering of ignition (interoceptive-precision modulation)
specification_sections.text:
Interoceptive-precision (Πⁱ) modulation predicts that ignition events cluster in time across multiple, dissociable timescales rather than at a single characteristic rate. This is the parameter-estimation core of Protocol 6: multi-timescale identifiability is the mathematical prerequisite for the nested (Russian-Doll) architecture, and its failure would collapse the hierarchy to a single ignition process. Two convergent criteria are required for full prediction confirmation:

Recovery (primary): A hierarchical multi-timescale Bayesian model, fit to the inter-ignition-interval series under Πⁱ modulation, recovers ≥ 3 dissociable clustering timescales — corresponding to the interoceptive/cortical temporal strata (τ_int,ℓ) of the APGI hierarchy. Recovery is assessed within the single-subject hierarchical Bayesian framework, with each dissociable timescale supported at BF₁₀ ≥ 6.

Dissociation: The multi-timescale model outperforms the best single-timescale alternative by Bayes Factor ≥ 100 (decisive evidence), confirming that the ≥ 3 timescales are jointly necessary rather than an over-parameterization of a single ignition rate.

Control for task structure: Because inter-ignition intervals are constrained by trial timing, block alternation and hit rate, the multi-timescale model is compared against 1,000 surrogate series that preserve each participant's trial timing, block structure and hit rate; a timescale counts as dissociable only if it is absent from ≥ 95% of surrogates.

This prediction is the decisive adversarial contrast with Global Neuronal Workspace Theory, which posits a single ignition timescale: recovery of ≥ 3 dissociable timescales under Πⁱ modulation is consistent with APGI's nested-timescale hierarchy (Multi-Scale paper, §2) and incompatible with a single-workspace broadcast model. Because Protocol 6 is designated Confirmatory-Exploratory, a confirmatory Pred 6.E result requires independent replication in ≥ 12 additional iEEG participants before it is used as standalone evidence for APGI; computational proxy data (Protocol 2) are exploratory and cannot substitute for replication.
specification_sections.role: source_context; curated structured decisions govern conflicts

specification_sections.heading: RT minimum at threshold rather than maximum (contradicts critical slowing) — Pred 6.C (behavioral)
specification_sections.text: AC1 shows no pre-stimulus increase on detected trials (group-median participant-level Kendall τ < 0.20 with the null supported at BF₀₁ ≥ 3) — Pred 6.C (electrophysiological); results in 0.20 ≤ τ < 0.40 are inconclusive and carry no falsifying weight

specification_sections.heading: Coherence unrelated to detection (r < 0.2) — Pred 6.D
specification_sections.text: Only a single ignition timescale is identifiable, or the single-timescale model is favored over the multi-timescale model (BF₀₁ ≥ 6) — Pred 6.E

specification_sections.heading: Limitations and Mitigation
specification_sections.text: Three limitations constrain Protocol 6 (Ignition-iEEG). First, sample size is small (target N = 20, minimum N = 12, of whom an estimated 8–15 will have adequate frontoparietal coverage), limiting statistical power. Second, electrode placement follows clinical rather than experimental criteria, creating unsystematic site variability. Third, generalizability is restricted: epilepsy patients may exhibit altered attractor dynamics relative to healthy populations. Mitigation strategies address each limitation directly — within-subject analyses dominate; trials with interictal spikes are excluded; surface EEG from healthy controls provides qualitative validation; and mechanistic conclusions require a minimum of two patients with bilateral frontoparietal plus anterior-insula coverage (the latter required for the Πⁱ modulation of Pred 6.E).
specification_sections.role: source_context; curated structured decisions govern conflicts

specification_sections.heading: Integration note
specification_sections.text: Protocol 6 (Ignition-iEEG) is the framework's highest-resolution test and its most constrained in generalizability. Confirmation of Pred 6.A–Pred 6.C jointly (bimodality + rapid transitions + critical slowing) would constitute the strongest available evidence for phase-transition dynamics in conscious access — a result that would simultaneously challenge graded-accumulation models and provide a mechanistic substrate for the ignition equation's threshold dynamics. Failure of Pred 6.C (critical slowing absent) while Pred 6.A/Pred 6.B confirm would suggest attractor dynamics without bifurcation — a partial result requiring theoretical revision of the θₜ adaptation rule. Pred 6.E is logically separable from this phase-transition triad: it tests the nested-hierarchy commitment (multi-timescale identifiability) rather than bistability per se, so it can confirm or fail independently of Pred 6.A–6.D.
specification_sections.role: source_context; curated structured decisions govern conflicts

specification_sections.heading: Exclusion thresholds
specification_sections.text: Trials contaminated by interictal epileptiform discharges within ±500 ms of stimulus onset will be excluded; participants for whom more than 30% of trials are excluded will be withdrawn from primary analyses and reported separately. These thresholds are set a priori and will not be adjusted post-hoc.
specification_sections.role: source_context; curated structured decisions govern conflicts

specification_sections.heading: Statistical Analysis
specification_sections.text:
AC1 is computed as the lag-1 autocorrelation of the high-gamma (70–150 Hz) amplitude envelope within consecutive 50 ms windows spanning the −500 to 0 ms pre-stimulus epoch (subsequently detected vs. undetected trials). The high-gamma envelope is down-sampled to 100 Hz before AC1 is computed in each 50-ms window. At 100 Hz a 50-ms window contains only five envelope samples. Before this AC1 statistic is confirmatory, archive simulations of its finite-sample bias, signal autocorrelation, trial pooling, participant-level uncertainty and group-median τ power. Specify whether AC1 is estimated within each trial and then pooled, or through an explicitly defined ensemble estimator; trial boundaries are never concatenated as adjacent time samples. If the estimator is not recoverable under these settings, Pred 6.C is deferred pending a prospective estimator/window amendment.

The trend statistic is Kendall's τ computed within each participant across the ten windows (n = 10 windows per participant); the group criterion is the median participant-level τ across the N = 20 participants (τ ≥ 0.40 confirms; τ < 0.20 with BF₀₁ ≥ 3 falsifies). Participant-level τ is compared between detected and non-detected trials by a permutation test with 10,000 permutations. Single-subject inference uses a hierarchical Bayesian model with participant-level random effects and partial pooling across the N = 20 target sample (BF₁₀ ≥ 6 per sub-prediction per participant); group-level inference applies Benjamini–Yekutieli FDR at q = 0.05.

methods_source_sections.heading: Outliers and influence
methods_source_sections.text:
4.3.2 Outlier and influential-observation policy

All rules below are fixed pre-collection and apply to every protocol unless a protocol body specifies otherwise; no post-hoc outlier rule may be introduced. (a) Trial level. Scalp-EEG trials exceeding the 150 µV peak-to-peak criterion (§4.2.1) are rejected; iEEG trials follow the interictal-discharge and |z| > 6 rule of §Protocol 6; behavioral trials in speeded detection tasks with RT < 150 ms or > 3 s are rejected as anticipations or lapses (Protocol 2 IGT and Protocol 7 bedside tasks use the rules in their protocol bodies). No further trial-level trimming is permitted. (b) Participant level. A participant is excluded only for a pre-registered admissibility failure (> 30% trial rejection, Data-Admissibility Gate; failed manipulation check; protocol violation). Statistical outlyingness is never itself an exclusion ground. (c) Observation level in models. Continuous predictors and outcomes are winsorized at ±3 SD within participant before entry into any confirmatory model; the untrimmed analysis is reported alongside as a mandatory sensitivity analysis, and a discrepancy in the confirmatory decision between the two is reported as an instability flag. (d) Influence. For every confirmatory regression or mixed model, Cook's distance is computed and observations with D > 4/n are reported; the model is refit without them as a sensitivity analysis. The trimmed refit is never the confirmatory result. (e) Model diagnostics and fallback. Gaussian models use the registered residual diagnostics; binary/ordinal generalized models use distribution-appropriate simulation or predictive diagnostics, not a Shapiro–Wilk residual gate. Appendix C must identify the exact estimator, tuning constants, inferential test and Bayesian evidence computation for each permitted fallback before lock. A fallback not so specified is a sensitivity analysis and cannot replace the primary confirmatory estimator.

methods_source_sections.heading: Bayesian prior sensitivity
methods_source_sections.text:
Sensitivity analyses

All confirmatory Bayesian conclusions are re-run under fixed prior transformations. Normal and HalfNormal priors: scale multiplied by 2 and by ½, location and support unchanged. Beta(2, 5) prior on η_RL: mean (2/7) preserved and concentration (sum of shape parameters, 7) multiplied by 2 and by ½, giving Beta(4, 10) and Beta(1, 2.5). Fixed parameters remain fixed or vary over a separately registered grid. Every evidence and interval criterion is recomputed under each sensitivity prior; if a conclusion crosses a §3.5.2 decision boundary (BF₁₀ = 3 or 100, BF₀₁ = 6), it is reported as prior-sensitive and reclassified as exploratory.

methods_source_sections.text:
Protocol 6 (Ignition-iEEG) — Clinical Intracranial Recordings

Status: Research approval pending. The research ethics committee, institution, approval identifier, date and protocol version will be recorded in a timestamped addendum once obtained, and recruitment does not begin before then. Clinical-care authorization for electrode implantation is separate and does not establish approval for this research.
Committee: Protocol is registered as a planned study and the registration will be amended with committee name, institution, approval number and date before any participant is approached.
Patient population: Epilepsy surgery candidates with clinically indicated intracranial electrode implants. Recordings conducted as part of standard clinical care; additional research analysis requires separate informed consent or waiver.
Informed consent: Separate consent for research-use analysis of clinical iEEG data, with right to decline without affecting clinical care.
